clue.text: Knock over tin? Leave Charlie a brandy

indicators.note: to knock something over is to topple it, so the run of pieces is turned end to end

parts.note: a tin is a can
to leave is to go
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone topples a tin and leaves their friend Charlie a bottle of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock over' turns the whole run CAN + GO + C backwards, giving C-OG-NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a type of French brandy from the Charente region, named after its home town.

clue.text: With head in clouds, put down a larger sum for a sword

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to lay is to put down
more means a greater amount

explanation.surface: A dreamer with head in the clouds puts down more money for a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLAYMORE is a large Scottish two-handed broadsword.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a Scottish broadsword, an example of a sword.

clue.text: Georgia, with upset stomach, gets the full range

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: Georgia, suffering a stomach upset, goes through every symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the complete range or scope of something.

clue.text: Turn, holding mug and a tumbler

indicators.note: holding means the stage word keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a turn is a short stage performance, an act
to mug is to rob

explanation.surface: A man turns while holding a mug and a glass tumbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is an acrobat who performs somersaults and flips.

clue.text: In the direction of remote Scottish town

parts.note: for can mean towards, as in 'heading for home'
remote means far away

explanation.surface: A remote Scottish town lies off in some direction.
explanation.walkthrough: FORFAR is a town in Angus in eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfar is the county town of Angus, a real place in Scotland.

clue.text: Instrument with blade in adult carries around

indicators.note: the blade word carries the abbreviation for around inside it

parts.note: an oar's flat end is its blade, so a blade can stand for oar
C, for circa, means around or about
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An instrument with a blade is carried around by an adult.
explanation.walkthrough: An OCARINA is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small wind instrument, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Lodge member, generous male when working

parts.note: free can mean generous, as in free with money
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
on means working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A lodge member is a generous man while at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so a member of a Masonic lodge is one.

clue.text: Ignore foggy district

indicators.note: foggy means confused, so the letters of the word are muddled

explanation.surface: People ignore a district shrouded in fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or district.

clue.text: Said after skin cream comes from castle

indicators.note: after places the spoken word behind the cream in the answer

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment for the skin
oral means spoken, said rather than written

explanation.surface: A skin cream is said to come from a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the royal family's estate and castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle is the British monarch's Scottish residence, an example of a castle.

clue.text: Day an old man ordered a Beatles record

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: On some day an old man ordered a Beatles single.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Madonna was a 1968 Beatles single.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Madonna is a song released by the Beatles, an example of one of their records.

clue.text: Settle a score against English in outskirts of Airdrie

indicators.note: in puts the other pieces inside the pair of outer letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone seeks revenge on the English on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Airdrie is a town near Glasgow; its outer letters A and E enclose V + ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a score is to take revenge for a wrong, a close idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Leave out some from Italy

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone decides to leave out a few things that came from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to fail to include it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Chap married in lodge back here in Cornwall

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person, a chap

indicators.note: back says the word for lodge is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to lodge is to room, to stay as a lodger

explanation.surface: A married man lodges somewhere back in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: BODMIN MOOR is a granite moorland in north-east Cornwall; the definition points to a place in that county.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodmin Moor is a well-known stretch of upland in Cornwall, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Soldier intends to get an income from investments

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: A soldier plans to earn money from his investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means is the idiom for unearned income from investments or inheritance, not a salary.

clue.text: Grant UFOs have crashed round Cuba's capital

indicators.note: round means the anagram goes around the next piece
crashed means wrecked, so the letters of these words are smashed into a new order
a capital is a first, upper-case letter, so take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: UFOs crash-land around the capital of Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges UFOSHAVE into VOUHSAFE, and 'round' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouchsafe is to grant or bestow something graciously.

clue.text: Moving home, a former Poet Laureate

parts.note: to be at home is to be in
Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: A former Poet Laureate is moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: In motion means moving, not stationary.

clue.text: Fully functional, like an athlete in training first thing?

definitions.meaning: working properly and operating, as a new system once launched

definitions.text: like an athlete in training first thing?
definitions.meaning: read literally, out of bed and jogging early in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means operating normally; literally an early trainer is out of bed and running.

clue.text: Almost applaud line about a naval officer

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to applaud is to admire

explanation.surface: Someone nearly applauds a line about a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line about a' asks for L to go with A, and the answer puts A first; L cannot literally surround a single letter, so 'about' only loosely means 'next to' here.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a high-ranking naval officer commanding a fleet.

clue.text: Novel written in July's session

indicators.note: written in says the answer is set down inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A novel was written during a July session.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses is James Joyce's famous novel, an example of a novel.

clue.text: Completely enthusiastic about spinner? Not quite

indicators.note: about places the enthusiasm word around the shortened toy

parts.note: to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: not quite means the word is one letter short, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: Someone is completely enthusiastic about a spinning toy, but not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' is a clipping signal applied to the spinning toy, and 'about' wraps the enthusiasm word around what is left; the surface's 'not quite' seems to qualify the enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is a Latin phrase meaning entirely or completely.

clue.text: Wearing them, one close to royalty must be rich

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take its last letter

explanation.surface: Anyone close to the royals who wears those things must be wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the money is an idiom for being wealthy or well off.

clue.text: Gunpowder, for one, left in container

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the container

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Gunpowder is left inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605 was a failed attempt to blow up the English Parliament; 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot is a famous conspiracy, an example of a scheme of that kind.

clue.text: Finished the last of the dough

parts.note: something finished is past

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has finished the last of the dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a soft moist mixture, as dough is, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Popular expression? Nonsense

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand
an air is an expression of manner, a look or demeanour

explanation.surface: A popular saying turns out to be nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is an idiom for empty talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Two brutes with it, hitman

parts.note: a brute can be a beast; an ass is a beast of burden, and two of them are wanted
a brute can be a beast; an ass is a beast of burden, and two of them are wanted
with it means fashionable, which is also in

explanation.surface: Two thugs team up with a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer, a synonym of hitman.

clue.text: US playwright, single, not in good health

parts.note: single means one
unwell is ill

explanation.surface: An American dramatist, unmarried and in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was an American playwright, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill is a celebrated American dramatist, an example of a US playwright.

clue.text: Behind a US violinist, Isaac

parts.note: Isaac Stern was a famous American violinist

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind the American violinist Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for behind or towards the rear of a vessel.
